newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK protesters closer to demonstration permission.
newsitem.headline: HK protesters closer to demonstration permission.

text.p: Pro-democracy protesters appear closer to gaining permission to demonstrate during this British colony's handover to Communist China on June 30, Democratic Party member Lee Wing-tat said on Saturday.

Beijing-appointed Chief Executive-designate, Tung Chee-hwa, appeared to have become more positive about letting protesters enter the colonial legislature building after a midnight handover ceremony to read out statements, Lee said on a radio programme.
"We notified (Tung's office) of the full details of our action plans for June 30-July 1. And this time we got a more positive response," he said.
"We hope that we can very peacefully get into the building and deliver our speech from the balcony," Lee said.
The legislature, where the Democrats hold the largest number of seats, will be dissolved at midnight on June 30 and a pro-Beijing assembly sworn in shortly thereafter.
The Democratic Party has refused to take part in the new assembly, which will pass laws until elections are held in 1998.
It has vowed to occupy the legislature building and read out protests while the new pro-Beijing assembly is being sworn in by Tung at a nearby convention centre in the early hours of July 1.

"We have explained to them our detailed operation and also they expressed some worries and we tried our best to give some comfort to their worries. So that I think the response from them this time is much better," Lee said.
The plans to occupy the legislature have threatened to pose the first real challenge for Tung from Hong Kong's pro-democracy campaigners.
Tung's office said on Saturday that discussions were continuing with the Democrats but no decision had been taken.
"Members of the Democratic Party have been in contact with the Chief Executive-designate's office and the matter is still under discussion," a spokesman for Tung said.
